Internal notes / quick triage:
- I tested the invite flow against Coupa with a similar partner link and captured the accept endpoint logs. I'm attaching a sanitized extract (coupa-accept-logs.txt).
- Observed behavior: accept endpoint returns a 302 -> redirect to our relay handler, then client sees a 409 on the final accept step when the relaystate contains a timestamp in vendor-local tz.
- Hypothesis: some vendor mail clients (or forwarding services) rewrite the query string (URL encoding) which ends up double-encoding the relaystate timestamp. Coupa's token TTL validator then parses it as expired (negative TTL) and returns an opaque error to the browser.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Resend activation with extended ttl (we can set TTL to 72h) and use our resend API that forces unencoded relaystate.
2) If resend fails, we can do a manual account claim: internal tool will call Coupa's admin API to mark the invite as accepted and return the supplier ID. That requires confirmation of HexWave's business name + last 4 of tax id.

I can run option (1) now. I put a sample payload in resend_payload.json. Karthik, any SAML caveats you want to add?

Ben Carter

Adding a quick SAML/relaystate note:
- Coupa's relay handler expects URL-safe base64 for relaystate. If a mail client wraps/escapes characters (plus signs, equals) it's possible the web server path auto-decodes once and leaves percent-encoded sequences that our handler then treats as literal. That can flip the embedded timestamp from e.g. 2026-09-25T15:00:00Z to an invalid parse.
- Also seen timezone skew where vendor systems produce timestamps without timezone markers and client-side parsing assumes local tz — that can make a perfectly valid 15:00 UTC token appear expired if interpreted as local.

Action: Ben, go ahead with the resend with TTL=72h. If HexWave still sees error, escalate to Coupa support (CASE-91234) and include the two sample log snippets I attached. Request they treat this as an invite-token parsing/relaystate issue — their team can confirm with their admin logs.
